segmentation_method.summary: k-means cluster analysis by YouGov data scientists with More in Common, on core-belief and group-identity items only; no demographic or party-ID variables were used to form the segments. The report describes the core-beliefs model as covering six dimensions and says segments were found from 45 questions about core beliefs, group belonging and political behaviour.

dimensions.name: Moral foundations
dimensions.detail: Abridged Moral Foundations Questionnaire, developed with Sean Stevens and Jonathan Haidt: care, fairness, authority, purity, loyalty (no liberty).

dimensions.name: Authoritarian disposition (parenting styles)
dimensions.detail: Child-rearing trait pairs (MacWilliams/Stenner approach), aggregated into an index from -1 to 1.

dimensions.name: Threat perception
dimensions.detail: 'Most people can be trusted'; 'the world is becoming a more and more dangerous place'; 'the area where I live is becoming more dangerous'.

dimensions.name: Personal agency and responsibility
dimensions.detail: Three 4-point paired items on individual effort v circumstance.

dimensions.name: Identity, tribalism and group affiliation / group favouritism (victimhood)
dimensions.detail: Importance and pride in group identities; views on who is favoured or mistreated in society.

segmentation_method.note_on_count: The task brief mentions five core-belief areas; the report itself lists six dimensions (p34 lists group identity, group favouritism, threat, parenting/authoritarianism, moral foundations, personal agency; p69 lists moral foundations, authoritarianism, threat, agency, political values, identity). Progressive Activists.summary: Highly educated, urban, working-age cosmopolitans whose politics is central to who they are. They see Britain through structural injustice (race, gender, class, wealth), are the most pessimistic about the country's direction, the most pro-immigration and the least patriotic, and they are by far the most vocal on social media. Strongest Remain group. Low threat perception, lowest authoritarianism, and moral concern focused almost entirely on care and fairness.

Civic Pragmatists.summary: Well-informed but not ideological, mostly women, and spread evenly across ages. Their worldview rests on concern for others' welfare, at home and abroad: almost all give to charity regularly. They are socially liberal, pro-immigration and pro-climate action, yet perceive more threat than Progressive Activists. More than most they are worn out by political division and value compromise, consensus, democracy and community.

Backbone Conservatives.summary: Older, wealthier, mostly white, rural and small-town Conservatives: proud, nostalgic about history, the monarchy and the armed forces, and the only segment where most think the country is heading the right way. Strong Leavers, keen consumers of traditional news, secure and high in trust and local agency. They put individual responsibility first, back spending cuts, are least worried about inequality and racism and negative on immigration; they back gradual rather than radical climate action and give all moral foundations similar weight.
